figures.finding: Nauru has no general income tax on individuals; pay and service fees bear the Employment and Services Tax: a resident pays nothing on the first $9,240 a month ($4,257 a fortnight, $2,129 a week) and 20% above.
figures.applies: Resident individuals; rates sheet 2023-24, thresholds restated in the 2024-25 guide

sources.said: (1) The rates of employment tax applicable to a resident individual are: (a) for a monthly pay period: Monthly Employment Income Rate $0 – $9,240 0% Above $9,240 20% (b) for a fortnightly pay period: Fortnightly Employment Income Rate $0 – $4,257 0% Above $4,257 20% (c) for a weekly pay period: Weekly Employment Income Rate $0 – $2,129 0% Above $2,129 20%
(3) The rates of services tax applicable to a resident individual are: (a) for a monthly payment period: Monthly Services Income Rate $0 – $9,240 0% Above $9,240 20%
Residents of Nauru including resettled refugees will not be charged tax if they earn less than $2,129 per week; $4,257 per fortnight; or $9,240 per month.

figures.finding: The payer deducts employment or services tax at each payment and remits it by the 15th of the next month; the tax deducted is final and employees and service providers file no return.
figures.applies: Employers and payers of service fees

sources.said: Both employment tax and service tax must be deducted by the payer at the time the employment income or service fee is paid which must be then paid to the Nauru Revenue Office by the 15th day of the following month.
No return is necessary from employees or service providers. The tax deducted is a final liability.

figures.finding: A non-resident providing services in Nauru pays 20% services tax on every dollar (30% for the Regional Processing Centre; 0% on the first $20,000 a year for those contracted by the Republic), and it is final.

sources.said: (4) The rates of services tax applicable are (a) for non-resident persons providing services to or in connection with the Regional Processing Centre is 30%; (b) for non-resident individuals providing services to the Republic where annual services income is: (i) 0 -$20,000 – rate is 0%; and (ii) above $20,000.00 – rate is 20%; and (c) for any other non-resident person providing services is 20%.
No return is necessary from employees or service providers. The tax deducted is a final liability.

figures.finding: The financial year runs from 1 July to 30 June; payers file an annual withholding return within 15 days of its end.

sources.said: complete an annual withholding tax return summarizing payments and tax deducted. The return is due within 15 days of the end of the financial year;

figures.finding: Every employer and employee in Nauru pays into the Nauru Superannuation Scheme: the employee 5% of superannuable salary and the employer 10% from 1 February 2026 (5% before), small employers of five or fewer employees with turnover under $10,000 and assets under $5,000 exempt.
figures.applies: Employees under the Nauru Superannuation Act 2019 as amended (passed 23 December 2025).

sources.said: It is a defined contribution scheme with employer contributions initially set at 5 per cent of superannuable salary and matching 5 per cent employee contribution. In the 2025-26 Budget there was an increase in the Employers contribution from 5% to 10%. This amendment was passed on the 23 December 2025 sitting and becomes effective from 1 February 2026. Super contributions are now mandatory for all employers and employees under the change. There are specific exemptions for small employers of five or less employees with an annual turnover of less than $10,000 and gross assets of less than $5,000

figures.finding: Nauru has no VAT or GST: the laws its Revenue Office administers are the Revenue Administration Act, the Employment and Services Tax Act, the Business Tax Act, the Telecommunications Service Tax Act (10% on telecom providers' gross sales) and the Gaming Act, so a freelancer's fee bears no consumption tax.
figures.applies: Taxes administered by the Nauru Revenue Office, 2026; customs duties at the border are not covered.

sources.said: Revenue Administration Act (RAA) Employment and Services Tax Act (ESTA) Business Tax Act (BTA) Telecommunications Service Tax Act Gaming Act 2011 … This Act imposes telecommunications service tax on a service provider at a rate of 10% in respect of the gross sales of telecommunication services
